newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil little changed in subdued markets.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil little changed in subdued markets.

text.p: NWE fuel oil markets ended the week with a whimper with stable prices and little business concluded, traders said.
High sulphur barges traded early in the day at $98 and $97.50 fob ARA for prompt material, while early February barrels changed hands at $102. Bunker demand was poor.

High sulphur cif cargoes failed to move far from barge numbers as an industry function stifled trade. A little pressure was seen coming from an offer of 50,000 tonnes of U.S.-origin material, which was thought still on offer on Friday.

Utility buying was lacklustre although some interest was thought still to be coming from Scotland. This demand pre-dates news of an outage at one unit at a Scottish nuclear power station. The brief outage was not expected to boost U.K. demand for fuel oil.
Low sulphur fuel oil was steady to weaker, and prompt material continues to overhang the market.

No fresh cargo deals were heard after two pieces, one out of Germany and the other out of the U.K., were sold to traders on Thursday. At least one of these cargoes is thought still on offer. Another trader with a commitment into Italy was heard seeking one cargo for early February.
